title: Kling Image 4.0: native 8K AI images, long text and 10-image sets
headline_html: Kling Image 4.0 brings native 8K to AI images
seo_title: Kling Image 4.0: Native 8K AI Image Model Launch
description: Kling Image 4.0 launched on 17 November with native 8K output, up to 2,000 characters of text per image and sets of 10 matching images. What brands get.
dek: Kuaishou's Kling AI has launched Kling Image 4.0, an image model it says is the first to generate at native 8K. It also handles long blocks of text and can create up to 10 consistent images from one prompt. It is live in Kling's app and API, though the headline claims come from Kling itself.

card.headline: Kling Image 4.0 brings *native 8K* AI images
points: Native 8K output, which Kling calls an industry first
Up to 2,000 characters of editable text in one image
Up to 10 matching images from a single prompt

tldr: Kling AI launched Kling Image 4.0 on 17 November 2026.
Kling says it is the first AI image model to output at native 8K resolution.
It can place up to 2,000 characters of text in one image, and the text and font can be edited after the image is made.
One prompt can produce a set of up to 10 images that keep the same characters, style and layout.
It is available now in Kling's Creative Studio and through its API; Kling has not published separate pricing for it.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Kling AI, the generative video and image business of Chinese tech company Kuaishou, released Kling Image 4.0 on 17 November 2026. It is the company's new image model, launched a month after its Kling 4.0 video model.

Kling's main claim is resolution: it says Image 4.0 is the first model in the industry to generate images natively at 8K, rather than making a smaller image and upscaling it. The release also focuses on two things that usually trip up image models: long text inside an image, and keeping several images consistent with each other.

sections.heading: The key details
list: Text in images: up to 2,000 characters in a single image, with the wording and font style editable after the image is generated.
Languages for text: reported support for English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese and simplified and traditional Chinese.
Image sets: up to 10 images from one prompt that keep the same characters, visual style and layout.
Where to use it: live in the Kling Creative Studio and through the Kling API from launch day.
Rankings: Kling says a preview version holds a leading spot on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard for text-to-image and image editing.
Price: Kling has not published a separate price for Image 4.0; it runs on the platform's existing credit system.

sections.heading: The background
paragraphs: Kling became known for video. Its Kling 4.0 video model arrived in mid-October with clips of up to 30 seconds, and the company has been building out a full creative suite around it. A strong image model matters for that suite because many AI videos start from a still frame.

Independent outlets covering the launch point out that the 8K, 2,000-character and 10-image claims all come from Kling's own announcement and have not yet been tested at scale by outside reviewers. Early hands-on results will show how well the text and consistency hold up in real work.

sections.heading: What it means for brands
sections.label: Papad Pixels view
paragraphs: Two features stand out for marketing teams. Sets of 10 consistent images make it much easier to build a whole campaign, such as a carousel or a run of product posts, around one look instead of fixing mismatched images by hand. Reliable long text means posters, menus and packaging mock-ups with real copy, not the garbled lettering AI images are known for.

8K is useful for print and large screens, but most social ads never need it, so test the claims on your own brief before switching tools. As an AI video production studio we often start a film from a key frame, so a sharper, more consistent image model feeds straight into the video. Read how the video side launched in our Kling 4.0 story, or see our AI video ads.

faq.a: Kling AI released Kling Image 4.0 on 17 November 2026, about a month after its Kling 4.0 video model.

faq.q: Does Kling Image 4.0 really make 8K images?
faq.a: Kling says it generates at native 8K and calls this an industry first. Outside reviewers have not yet confirmed the claim at scale.

faq.q: Where can I use Kling Image 4.0?
faq.a: It is available in the Kling Creative Studio and through the Kling API. Kling has not published a country-by-country list.

faq.q: How much does Kling Image 4.0 cost?
faq.a: Kling has not announced a separate price for Image 4.0; it uses Kling's existing credit-based plans.
